DERIVED artifact: AEP_DATA is generated from the finished storyboard as a late build step (proposed id aep_profile) - each touchpoint becomes an event, each revealed detail a field, each stitched id an identity, each qualifying behaviour a segment, all tagged with the story checkpoint. Drop at every 'cut to the platform' beat and call AEP.setStep(k).
screens.description: Adobe Experience Platform Real-Time Customer Profile panel, exact match to the KSIA reference, upgraded 20 Jul 2026 to the full timeline plus progressive story-time. Adobe Experience Cloud header; REAL-TIME CUSTOMER PROFILE band with customer-profile (photo, fields, consent checks), identity (Desktop/Mobile/Email/ECID/CRM IDs) and segmentation cards; EXPERIENCE EVENTS band with an icon interaction grid on dotted timelines (web/email/mail-open/phone/mirror/qr). Adobe product UI in FIXED dark neutrals (Adobe-surface exception), data-only via AEP_DATA. Every field, identity, segment and event carries a step (the story checkpoint that first captured it); AEP.setStep(n)/next()/prev()/all() shows the profile AS IT STOOD at that checkpoint with newly captured items glowing in, so a deck can cut to it at several points in the journey and each time it holds only what has been captured so far. On load it renders the full profile. Use on every 'cut to the platform' orchestration beat of a journey deck.

components.description: The agentic workplan rail as a reusable token-driven element (T1 of the interactive backlog): plan title, status line (planned / running step n / done, held for your approval), step counter pill, 4-6 named steps with agent badges that tick through on a timer with a working indicator, and staggered artifact cards on completion. Drive it with WPR.run()/WPR.step(n)/WPR.reset() or the optional on-stage buttons. Use on the agentic beat of any customer story; the Coworker demo remains the Adobe-surface variant.
components.note: NO global key bindings by design: arrows belong to deck navigation, drive via the API. All copy in WPR_DATA; colour only from role tokens (verified: done-state takes --brand under a Monzo token set). Cadence via --wpr-cadence.

components.description: One page, morphed per persona (T4 of the interactive backlog): a browser-framed page whose hero, offer pill, three product cards and notification toast all swap in place when a persona chip is picked. Fade-swap engine with a transition lock and queued switches, so rapid clicking never glitches; layout is pixel-stable, only content and colour change. Drive with the chips or PSW.set(i)/next()/prev()/reset(). Use for the same-moment-three-customers beat of any personalisation story.
components.note: NO global key bindings by design. Persona art is token-derived gradients (zero image work on reskin); all copy and personas in PSW_DATA, the Maya/Dev/Priya trio is sample data.

components.description: The draggable before/after wipe (T3 of the interactive backlog): two identical scene compositions layered (copy block + message-on-device), a divider the presenter drags to reveal the after side, with snap points at 0/50/100 and double-click to recentre. The before side is a deliberately grey world; the after side takes the customer tokens, so the contrast IS the message. Drive by dragging or CWP.set(pct, snap)/CWP.reset(). Use for the one-blast-versus-one-moment beat that opens most stories.
components.note: NO document key bindings; the internal a11y range answers arrows only while presenter-focused. Before-side greys are hardcoded on purpose (outside the token contract); scenes and copy in CWP_DATA. Device mock is a generic rounded frame, no camera.

sources: claude-design-t2 (mechanics; the ROI-pitch frame was retired)
components.description: A generic live-number instrument (from T2 of the interactive backlog): data-defined sliders on the left, a big eased count-up outcome plus secondary outcomes on the right, any math via VDL_DATA.compute, with an honest assumptions accordion. NOT an ROI calculator: we sell experience stories, not spreadsheet promises, so use it to make ONE story number playable (minutes given back, moments caught in time, orders rescued). Drive with the sliders or VDL.set(key, value)/reset()/values(). Kin: big-number-money-reveal is the animated payoff version; this is the playable version.
components.note: NO global key bindings; sliders answer arrows only while presenter-focused. Inputs clamp (range attrs + guarded reads, no NaN paths). All ranges, labels, formats and the compute() live in VDL_DATA; sample data frames service time given back.

components.description: The closing-slide outcomes row: four stat tiles whose numbers count up (eased, decimals supported) when the strip enters view, or on PFS.play(); PFS.reset() re-arms it. Extracted from the field guide's library stat tiles because every deck was rebuilding the pattern by hand for its proof slide. Kin: big-number-money-reveal is the single dramatic money moment; this is the row of smaller proofs.
components.note: PROOF IS NEVER INVENTED: shipped values must be the customer's own case numbers or a cited benchmark; the banked numbers are placeholder shapes only. If there is no honest number, cut the tile. NO key bindings.

components.description: The two-act story played in sync (T15 of the interactive backlog): the customer's moment on the left, the system behind it on the right, one beat stepper driving both from a single state index so they can never desync. Each advance sends a hot pulse down a rounded-elbow wire and the product card lights only when the pulse arrives, so cause visibly precedes effect; finished cards settle to quiet ticks as the right pane accumulates history. Drive with the dots or TAS.go(n)/next()/prev()/play()/reset(). Use for the replay-with-the-machinery-showing beat: act two of a two-act story, or the how-Adobe-did-it moment after any journey plays.
components.note: NO global key bindings. Left pane takes the customer tokens; the right pane is a fixed Adobe-neutral inset (blue #3B63FB) BY DESIGN, outside the token contract. Wires measure the live layout; if mounted hidden, call TAS.layout() after reveal. Beats, products, copy and every duration live in TAS_DATA.

components.description: The fork moment (T16 of the interactive backlog): a setup line, three choice chips, and a branch that plays in place. The picked chip sweeps to the brand colour while the others shrink to quiet also-possible pills, a wire draws itself to the outcome card (clip-path reveal, staggered rows), and Continue-the-story collapses the branch into a one-line trace pill that rides the spine with ONE merge pulse. Drive with the chips or CHB.choose(i)/rejoin()/reset(); re-choosing reverses fast and never shows two branches. Use for live-room participation (ask the audience, click what they shout), discovery workshops (pick the promise with the customer), and interactive demos; NOT for narrated linear decks, whose spine is fixed on purpose.
components.note: NO global key bindings. Wire maths is scale-proof (client-rect deltas converted to viewBox units), so the panel survives transform:scale() deck mounts. All copy, choices, the trace template and every duration in CHB_DATA; the fulfilment trio is sample data.

components.description: The right-message-right-moment beat as one living phone (T14 of the interactive backlog): a locked phone wakes, the push drops in with an overshoot and one ring pulse, then on open the notification lifts up and off the screen while the lock clock blurs away and a real product screen builds in beneath it (app bar with the brand logo, product photo and a back-in-stock pill, product name and price, selectable size or spec chips, an availability or delivery card, one action), its sections cascading; the action draws its check with a soft pulse and slides the confirmation and receipt up. Presenter-paced instead of a timed animation: the phone itself is the tap surface (tap to wake, tap the card, tap the action), or drive it with LPM.push()/open()/act()/play()/reset(). Fully data-driven and reskinnable: two banked sample shapes, home-restock (physical retail, in-store hold) and fashion-restock (online apparel, back-in-your-size with size chips and free delivery), picked via window.LPM_PRESET, or override the whole object via window.LPM_DATA (see demos/asos-living-phone for a real ASOS product-page instance). Use for the arriving-notification beat every journey story has: the Monzo nudge, the KSIA gate change, the Northwind reroute, or any retail back-in-stock or back-in-your-size moment.
components.note: NO global key bindings. Built by extraction after the T14 Design pass was rejected. Generic rounded frame, no camera dot, no notch (house rule + asset-licensing); a real bottom tab bar and home indicator complete the app chrome (bag tab shows a count once done). app slots: logo (app-bar mark), heroImage (product photo; else a token-gradient placeholder, where LICENSED photography drops in), eyebrow, options (strings or {label,active} size chips), callout {icon:pin|truck|clock|tag}, and followUp {icon,prompt,sub,cta,confirm} for an opt-in value offered after the action (the AJO beat, e.g. a reminder before a delivery cutoff; tapping confirms in place and never advances the phone). All copy and durations in LPM_DATA; play() uses a separate timer pool from manual calls so a mid-play tap cancels the take cleanly.
CSS gradients; replace/augment with licensed Adobe Stock darks when the Stock connector is live

components.description: Surface a detail panel ON DEMAND over the current scene instead of parking it permanently on the slide: a small trigger tab sits on the stage, clicking it dims and blurs the scene and slides the panel up, and the scrim or a Back-to-the-story close dismisses it. Built so journey decks stop nailing the live-profile / aep-xray to a fixed column - the scene stays clean and the platform is one click away when the presenter wants it. On a journey scene this frees the right side, so the DEVICE (phone/laptop/browser) grows large there; mount ONE banked aep-xray and call AEP.setStep(sceneN) per scene so it shows the profile as it stood at that checkpoint, never a per-slide profile column. Drive with the tab or PO.show()/hide()/toggle(); PO.body() returns the slot. Reusable for any pull-this-up moment (profile, ROI, an architecture inset, a proof panel).
components.note: PROFILE USE: mount the banked aep-xray inside .po-body (PO.body()) and call AEP.setStep(k) to the checkpoint so it holds only what has been captured so far; the sample stand-in is just so the element demos on its own. NO global key bindings. Trigger + sheet chrome reskin via role tokens; the mounted panel keeps its own styling (aep-xray stays a fixed Adobe surface). All copy in PO_DATA.

components.description: The interstitial / 'later' slide as a house pattern: narrative on the left (eyebrow, big title, supporting line) and a contextual image of the persona on the right, showing what they are doing at the START of the next scene (e.g. before an evening phone scene, a shot of her on the sofa on her phone). Replaces thin centred-text transitions so the persona stays present across the seams of the story. All copy in SXN_DATA; reskins via role tokens.
components.note: IMAGERY DISCIPLINE: the image slot defaults to a labelled FIREFLY PLACEHOLDER that names the exact shot to generate (never a broken box, never scraped stock). A deck sets image.src to the generated Firefly render and it drops straight in. asset-licensing.md: persona imagery is Firefly or a labelled placeholder. No script state, no key bindings.

Retail-bank app home: proactive shortfall nudge, current balance, recent transactions, move-money CTA. Reskins via role tokens.
Travel/airline app home: boarding-soon card, flight + lounge rows, fast-track/priority chips, boarding-pass CTA. Reskins via role tokens.
Retail/commerce app home: members edit, rewards-tier progress meter, basket + saved rows, checkout CTA. Reskins via role tokens.
Telco/utility app home: data-usage meter, next-bill, roaming + scam-shield actions. Reskins via role tokens.

Fully interactive Brand Concierge chat (clickable conversation tree): Agent Orchestrator rail (Site Advisory / Product Advisor / Order agents light per stage), product recommendations with live stock + why-lines, guided comparison table, in-chat one-tap checkout, and order-tracking timeline. Brand-governed messaging. Role-token reskinnable, offline, no deps. Use as a live demo segment mid-story (TODO 'customer demos mid-story'). Published artifact 15 Jul.

app_screens.description: Fully interactive Adobe Coworker demo in two views. View 1 is the banked screens/cx-enterprise-home (built from the real Figma source and asserted against it): type into the prompt bar or click a suggested chip. View 2 is the Coworker conversation: the prompt lands as a user message, Coworker names a WORKPLAN, steps back, and its 4-6 named steps tick through in mandatory CSC order (Planning, Workflow Ops, Creative Ideation with Firefly, Asset Mgmt, Delivery, Optimisation) with agent badges lighting per step, then artifacts land and quick-reply chips offer the follow-ups. Free text reroutes to the closest of three plans by keyword so the demo never dead-ends. Offline, no deps. Use on the Coworker/AI-home beat of a story.
app_screens.note: ADOBE PRODUCT UI: parameterize DATA ONLY (the SCRIPT/PLANS block in the script), never rebrand the chrome. GENERATED: edit screens/cx-enterprise-home or build_coworker.py and re-run it, never hand-edit the html. The chat panel is reconstructed from a screenshot (the saved page was React and only its shell survived), so unlike view 1 it is NOT design-exact.

Use for the 'she asks an AI assistant and the brand surfaces in the answer' moment (pairs with claude-chat).

app_screens.description: Noula-reskinned interactive Brand Concierge (sage+clay skincare tokens, Fraunces): the SKINCARE reskin example.
